title: Federal Open Market Committee announces approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy
summary: The FOMC unanimously approved updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy on August 22, 2025. This framework statement, originally adopted in 2012 and previously reviewed in 2019-20, was updated to reflect lessons from the past five years. The 2% longer-run inflation goal was explicitly not a focus of this review. The updates aim to enhance transparency, accountability, and effectiveness of monetary policy.
key_points: FOMC unanimously approved updates to its monetary policy framework statement on August 22, 2025
The 2025 review was announced in November 2024 and included Fed Listens events and a May 2025 research conference
The Committee's 2% longer-run inflation goal was not a focus of the review
Updates reflect lessons from the economy over the past five years
The statement emphasizes the Committee's commitment to maximum employment and stable prices
The full updated statement is available in PDF format but the specific content of updates is not detailed in this press release
why_it_matters: This framework statement serves as the foundation for FOMC policy actions and shapes how the Fed interprets its dual mandate. However, this press release announces the approval without detailing what actually changed. Market participants would need to review the full PDF statement to understand the substantive updates to Fed policy strategy. The fact that the 2% inflation goal was not a focus suggests the changes may relate more to the employment side of the mandate or the framework's implementation.
macro_context: The framework update reflects the Fed's ongoing effort to adapt its monetary policy strategy based on post-pandemic economic experience. The review process (Fed Listens events and research conference) suggests a deliberate, consultative approach to policy framework evolution.
